title: Safe macros
description:
Define these macros in `solution.c`. The tests use them inside bigger expressions, so every one needs its parentheses:

```c
MAX(a, b)            /* the larger value */
ABS(x)               /* the absolute value */
ARRAY_LEN(arr)       /* elements in an array declared in the same scope */
IS_EVEN(n)           /* 1 for even, 0 for odd */
CLAMP(x, lo, hi)     /* x kept between lo and hi */
STRINGIFY(x)         /* the argument's text as a string: STRINGIFY(a + b) is "a + b" */
```

starter.solution.c:
#define MAX(a, b) a > b ? a : b
#define ABS(x) x < 0 ? -x : x
#define ARRAY_LEN(arr) 0
#define IS_EVEN(n) 0
#define CLAMP(x, lo, hi) x
#define STRINGIFY(x) ""

solution.solution.c:
#define MAX(a, b) ((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))
#define ABS(x) ((x) < 0 ? -(x) : (x))
#define ARRAY_LEN(arr) (sizeof (arr) / sizeof (arr)[0])
#define IS_EVEN(n) ((n) % 2 == 0)
#define CLAMP(x, lo, hi) ((x) < (lo) ? (lo) : (x) > (hi) ? (hi) : (x))
#define STRINGIFY(x) #x

hints: Put brackets around every parameter and around the whole body: `#define MAX(a, b) ((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))`. Without them, `MAX(x, y) + 1` or `ABS(a - b)` go wrong.
`ARRAY_LEN(arr)` is `(sizeof(arr) / sizeof((arr)[0]))`, and `#x` in a macro body turns the argument into a string.
